harnessVariantIssue.definition: The harness variant issue element <harnessVariantIssue> contains the issue of a harness variant.
harnessVariantIssue.title: Harness issue

hotspot.definition: The element <hotspot> contains the definition of graphical regions in an illustration and contains information needed to navigate between graphical objects or between graphical objects and text. For use of the element <hotspot> in the context of a learning assessment, refer to Chap 3.9.5.2.13.5.
hotspot.title: Hotspot

hoursToOpen.definition: This element indicates the elapsed time necessary to open the access point.
hoursToOpen.title: Elapsed time to open the access point

identAndStatusSection.definition: The element <identAndStatusSection> is used to contain the identification and status of a data module/ publication module, which are captured in the two parts, identification and status.
identAndStatusSection.title: Identification and status section

identExtension.definition: The element <identExtension> establishes a producer unique subdomain for instance identification. The identification extension gives the additional parameters needed to establish a unique identification of a data module/ publication in those cases when data module code/ publication module, issue and in-work numbers together with the language and country are insufficient to form a universally unique identity.
identExtension.title: Identification extension

identNumber.definition: The element <identNumber> contains the manufacturer's identification information.
identNumber.title: Identification number

identSleeve.definition: The element <identSleeve> is contained in the list of identification sleeves element <identSleeveGroup>. The list of identification sleeves is a child element of the list of the standard parts element <standardPartGroup>.
identSleeve.title: Element <identSleeve> and child elements

if.definition: The element <if> is used to identify an "if" statement.
if.title: If statement

illustratedPartsCatalog.definition: The element <illustratedPartsCatalog> is used to contain the illustrated parts catalog information of a data module (excluding references).
illustratedPartsCatalog.title: Illustrated parts catalog

illustrationRef.definition: The illustration reference element <illustrationRef> contains references to other parts of the electrical system publications.
illustrationRef.title: Illustration reference

ilsNumber.definition: The element <ilsNumber> contains an interdisciplinary cross reference to an integrated logistic support number.
ilsNumber.title: Integrated logistic support number

impedance.definition: The element <impedance> contains the AC impedance of the wire material, normally of a cable.
impedance.title: Impedance

incorporation.definition: The element <incorporation> gives the incorporation status of technical conditions in the documentation.
incorporation.title: Incorporation status list

incorporationStatus.definition: The element <incorporationStatus> is used to define the status of the incorporation of a technical condition.
incorporationStatus.title: Incorporation status

indexFlag.definition: The element <indexFlag> is used to contain the text of an item that is required to be included in an automatically generated index.
indexFlag.title: Index

infoName.definition: The element <infoName> is linked to the information code using the attribute infoCode. Normally the information name is the short description of the information code. For example, information code 520 will have information name "Remove procedure". Projects can decide to modify (or extend) the information name to one that is more suitable, provided the sense of the information code is maintained. An example of where this could be used would be the information code 251 is "Clean procedures". A project can have a data module that tells the reader how to clean with water (this could be 251A) another data module could tell the reader how to clean with air (this could be 251B). In both cases, the information name can be extended from "Clean procedures" to "Clean procedures (clean with water)" and "Clean procedures (clean with air)".
infoName.title: Information name

initialize.definition: The element <initialize> is used to set an initial value for the variable using element <expression>.
initialize.title: Initialize

initialProvisioningProject.definition: The element <initialProvisioningProject> is used to store information regarding the Initial Provisioning Project (IPP).
initialProvisioningProject.title: Initial provisioning project number

initialProvisioningProjectRef.definition: The element <initialProvisioningProjectRef> is used to contain only a reference to another IPP for non-chapterized IPD (in an electronic (IPDP) it mainly will address the first CSN of this referenced IPPN).
initialProvisioningProjectRef.title: Refer to IPP

inlineSignificantData.definition: The element <inlineSignificantData> contains a significant meaning, such as a lubricant or manufacturer code.
inlineSignificantData.title: Paragraph significant data

inspection.definition: The element <inspection> groups the inspection limit information with the associated remark information.
inspection.title: Inspection information

inspectionDefinition.definition: This element contains information about inspections. Inspections are a way to group tasks that are related to the topic or intent of the inspection. This element groups a set of tasks with the limit information associated to perform the set of tasks.
inspectionDefinition.title: Inspection definition

inspectionType.definition: The element <inspectionType> provides a classification of maintenance into various types such as "systems", "structural" and "zonal".
inspectionType.title: Inspection type

installationInfo.definition: The element <installationInfo> contains electrical equipment installation information. The element is repeatable to cover multiple occurrence equipment.
installationInfo.title: Installation information

installationLocation.definition: The repeatable element <installationLocation> contains the installation location information of the equipment instances.
installationLocation.title: Installation location

interchangeability.definition: The element <interchangeability> is used to record the interchangeability of two or more items at the same location. This element will only be populated if the element <reasonForSelection> is not set to "0".
interchangeability.title: Interchangeability

internalRef.definition: The element <internalRef> is used to mark up a cross-reference from one point in a data module to another point in the same data module. This is achieved using the normal ID/IDREF mechanism, refer to Para 2.1.1.1.
internalRef.title: Internal reference

internet.definition: The element <internet> is repeatable and contains internet addresses for the business.
internet.title: Internet addresses

isolateDetectedFault.definition: The element <isolateDetectedFault > contains the information needed to isolate the detected fault to an LRU from amongst a list of suspected LRU. This is done by referring out to another data module through the element <faultIsolationRef> or by describing a test on these LRU using the element <lruItem>.
isolateDetectedFault.title: Isolate detected fault

isolatedFault.definition: The element <isolatedFault> is used to capture isolated faults information.
isolatedFault.title: Isolated faults

isolationInfo.definition: The element <isolationInfo> contains the diagnostic information for the observed fault. This is done by referring out using the element <faultIsolationRef> or by describing a diagnostic process using the element <diagnosticProcess> or simply testing the LRU using the element <lruItem>.
isolationInfo.title: Fault isolation information

isolationMainProcedure.definition: The element <isolationMainProcedure> contains the individual isolation steps.
isolationMainProcedure.title: Main isolation procedure

isolationProcedure.definition: The element <isolationProcedure> contains the isolation procedure including preliminary requirements and closeup requirements.
isolationProcedure.title: Isolation procedure

isolationProcedureEnd.definition: The element <isolationProcedureEnd> contains further isolation actions (these are either within the data module or referenced out to another data module) or to the element <closeRqmts> containing a closeup procedure.
isolationProcedureEnd.title: Isolation procedure end

isolationStep.definition: The element <isolationStep> contains the textual description of the action, the question and answer alternatives. It can also include eg a title, warnings, cautions and note.
isolationStep.title: Fault isolation step

isolationStepAnswer.definition: The element <isolationStepAnswer> contains the answers to the corresponding question (element <isolationStepQuestion>). The answers are given in the form of a reference to another action, to one or more final actions (in element <isolationProcedureEnd>) or to close-up requirements <closeRqmts>.
isolationStepAnswer.title: Answer

issueDate.definition: The element <issueDate> contains date information for the data module/ publication module. Every issue whether initially written, completely revised or updated by changes, must be allocated an ISO 8601 calendar date in the form YYYY-MM-DD.
issueDate.title: Issue date

issueInfo.definition: The element <issueInfo> contains the issue number of the data module/ publication module.
issueInfo.title: Issue information

itemDescr.definition: This element is used to contain the textual description of the father element.
itemDescr.title: Description

itemIdentData.definition: This element groups the properties that describe the part.
itemIdentData.title: Description data

itemNumber.definition: The element <itemNumber> is assigned to the checklist item for reference purposes. It is used to identify the line item or the row number for data presented in tabular format.
itemNumber.title: Item number

itemSequenceNumber.definition: The mandatory, repeatable element <itemSequenceNumber> is used to store the Item Sequence Number (ISN). It also contains elements which store metadata about the item.
itemSequenceNumber.title: Item sequence number

jobTitle.definition: The element <jobTitle> contains the job title of the individual contact.
jobTitle.title: Job title

language.definition: The element <language> is used to describe the language in which the data module/ publication module is written.
language.title: Language

lastName.definition: The element <lastName> contains the last name of the individual contact.
lastName.title: Last name

lcAge.definition: The element <lcAge> describes the learners’ age range.
lcAge.title: Age

lcAnswerOption.definition: The <lcAnswerOption> container element provides a single answer option for true-false, single-select, or multiple-select assessment interactions.
lcAnswerOption.title: Answer option

lcAnswerOptionContent.definition: The <lcAnswerOptionContent> container element provides the content and feedback for an answer option to a question, and can indicate that the option is correct or incorrect.
lcAnswerOptionContent.title: Answer option content

lcAnswerOptionGroup.definition: The <lcAnswerOptionGroup> container element provides answer options for true-false, single-select, or multiple-select assessment interactions.
lcAnswerOptionGroup.title: Answer option group

lcAssessment.definition: The element <lcAssessment> describes the manner in which the learning will be assessed. It is the high level design that captures how embedded, pre- and post-assessments will be employed.
lcAssessment.title: Assessment

lcAsset.definition: The <lcAsset> element is used to hold images and other graphic assets to support an assessment interaction.
lcAsset.title: Asset

lcAttitude.definition: The element <lcAttitude> describes the mental state that influences the choices of personal actions.
lcAttitude.title: Attitude

lcAudience.definition: The element <lcAudience> describes the learner's profile taking the instruction.
lcAudience.title: Audience

lcBackground.definition: The element <lcBackground> describes the learners’ professional background and the relevancy to the learning plan.
lcBackground.title: Background

lcChallenge.definition: The element <lcChallenge> describes student practice exercises. For example, if network diagrams are the subject matter, a challenge might be ?put this network into its proper sequence?.
lcChallenge.title: Challenge

lcCIN.definition: The element <lcCIN> provides an alpha-numeric alternate identifier to the project title.
lcCIN.title: Course Identification Number

lcClassroom.definition: The element <lcClassroom> describes technical aspects of the course to take place in a classroom.
lcClassroom.title: Classroom

lcClient.definition: The element <lcClient> provides the person or organization sponsoring or requiring the learning event development.
lcClient.title: Client

lcConstraints.definition: The element <lcConstraints> describes constraints imposed by the technologies used to create, distribute, deliver, and display the instruction. For example, if constraints are not met, the learner will not experience the instruction as designed. These must be considered in light of how the instruction will be used in relation to the learning objectives.
lcConstraints.title: Constraints

lcCorrectResponse.definition: The empty <lcCorrectResponse> element indicates a correct <lcOptionContent> response in a <lcAnswerOption>.
lcCorrectResponse.title: Correct response

lcDelivDate.definition: The element <lcDelivDate> provides the project delivery date.
lcDelivDate.title: Delivery Date

lcDelivery.definition: The element <lcDelivery> describes the instructional delivery methods and technologies. To maximize training effectiveness and optimize resource utilization, content developed should be founded upon needs and job task analysis data and leverage instructional delivery methods and technologies (eg, computer-based, web-based, video, performance support systems). A training delivery analysis includes review of the NLOS, identification and evaluation of available delivery options, and selection of the optimum delivery means.
lcDelivery.title: Delivery

lcDownloadTime.definition: The element <lcDownloadTime> describes the maximum time allowed for download time in the client’s delivery environment.
lcDownloadTime.title: Download Time

lcDuration.definition: The element <lcDuration> provides an estimated duration for the learning activity.
lcDuration.title: Duration

lcEdLevel.definition: The element <lcEdLevel> describes the range of learners’ education level and the relevancy to the learning plan.
lcEdLevel.title: Education Level

lcFeedback.definition: The <lcFeedback> element provides information to the learner about a correct or incorrect response during an interactive assessment.
lcFeedback.title: Feedback

lcFeedbackCorrect.definition: The <lcFeedbackCorrect> element provides feedback to the learner about a correct response in an assessment interaction.
lcFeedbackCorrect.title: Feedback correct

lcFeedbackIncorrect.definition: The <lcFeedbackIncorrect> element provides feedback to the learner about an incorrect response in an assessment interaction.
lcFeedbackIncorrect.title: Feedback incorrect

lcFileSizeLimitations.definition: The element <lcFileSizeLimitations> describes the file size limitations in the client’s delivery environment.
lcFileSizeLimitations.title: File Size Limitations

lcGapAnalysis.definition: The element <lcGapAnalysis> is the third high level container within the element <lcLearningPlan>. Analysis compares existing learning objectives to current job task analysis (JTA).
lcGapAnalysis.title: Gap Analysis

lcGapItem.definition: The element <lcGapItem> is a repeatable wrapper capturing gaps between existing training objectives and related job-task-analysis content.
lcGapItem.title: Gap Item

lcGapItemDelta.definition: The element <lcGapItemDelta> describes the gap between the learning objective and the job task analysis.
lcGapItemDelta.title: Gap Item Delta

lcGeneralDescription.definition: The element <lcGeneralDescription> provides a space to develop a general description about the organization’s training needs.
lcGeneralDescription.title: General Description

lcGoals.definition: The element <lcGoals> describes the outcomes desired by the organization to be addressed by the training effort. These goals may require concurrent efforts outside of training such as technology acquisition, reorganization, and so forth.
lcGoals.title: Goals

lcGraphics.definition: The element <lcGraphics> describes standards and system requirements for displaying graphics, 3D animations from CAD, navigation through virtual spaces, etc.
lcGraphics.title: Graphics

lcHotspot.definition: The hotspot interaction asks the assessment taker to click on a region of the screen to indicate a choice.
lcHotspot.title: Hotspot

lcHotspotMap.definition: This interaction designates an action area or region over an image, allowing a click in that region to get scored as correct or incorrect in response to an interaction question. Refer to Chap 3.9.5.2.1.8.
lcHotspotMap.title: Hotspot map

lcInstruction.definition: This element describes the specifics of a learning activity.
lcInstruction.title: Instruction

lcInteraction.definition: The repeatable container element <lcInteraction> provides the assessment question interactions.
lcInteraction.title: Interaction

lcIntervention.definition: The element <lcIntervention> is the fourth wrapper under the element <learningPlan>. It describes the approach and strategies to building the learning materials based on the element <lcNeedsAnalysis> content.
lcIntervention.title: Intervention

lcInterventionItem.definition: The element <lcInterventionItem> is a repeatable wrapper describing how learning content is built. It describes the systems approach to analyzing, designing, developing, implementing, and evaluating any instructional experience.
lcInterventionItem.title: Intervention Item

lcIntro.definition: The element <lcIntro> provides a detailed introduction and description of the content to be delivered, in cases where the <shortDescr> is not adequate to fully describe the content.
lcIntro.title: Introduction

lcItem.definition: The <lcItem> element contains content for an item that matches the matching item in a match table contained in a match table interaction.
lcItem.title: Item

lcJtaItem.definition: The element <lcJtaItem> provides the description of job task analysis as related to a particular learning objective.
lcJtaItem.title: Job Task Analysis Item

lcLearnStrat.definition: The element <lcLearnStrat> describes the manner in which the learning content will be instructed. It should be a high level design that applies instructional-design theories and models.
lcLearnStrat.title: Learning Strategy

lcLMS.definition: The element <lcLMS> describes the LMS name and version number.
lcLMS.title: LMS

lcMatching.definition: The matching interaction asks the assessment taker to link two related items together from a list of multiple options.
lcMatching.title: Matching

lcMatchingHeader.definition: The <lcMatchingHeader> container element provides column headings for items to be matched in a match table interaction.
lcMatchingHeader.title: Matching header

lcMatchingItem.definition: The <lcMatchingItem> element contains content for the matching side of a matching pair of items in a match table interaction.
lcMatchingItem.title: Matching item

lcMatchingPair.definition: The <lcMatchingPair> container element provides a table row with the pair of items that comprise a correct match in a matching interaction.
lcMatchingPair.title: Matching pair

lcMatchTable.definition: The <lcMatchTable> element contains a format for matching items in an assessment interaction.
lcMatchTable.title: Match table

lcModDate.definition: The element <lcModDate> provides the project modification date.
lcModDate.title: Modification Date

lcMotivation.definition: The element <lcMotovation> describes the reasons why the learners’ want and/or need to take the instruction.
lcMotivation.title: Motivation

lcMultipleSelect.definition: A multiple select interaction presents the assessment taker with a question and three or more possible answers, where two or more answers are correct.
lcMultipleSelect.title: Multiple select

lcNeeds.definition: The element <lcNeeds> describes the needs behind the outcomes described in the element <lcGoals>.
lcNeeds.title: Needs

lcNeedsAnalysis.definition: This is the second high level container element in the element <learningPlan>. It describes the training requirement and identifies the need to develop or revise content. These include periodic training gap analyses, changes to operational or maintenance requirements, and changes to equipment or systems.
lcNeedsAnalysis.title: Needs Analysis

lcNextSteps.definition: The element <lcNextSteps> describes the next steps to reinforce the knowledge learned.
lcNextSteps.title: Next steps

lcNoLMS.definition: The element <lcNoLMS> describes any technical requirements when SCORM and an LMS is not required.
lcNoLMS.title: NoLMS

lcObjective.definition: The element <lcObjective> describes a single learning objective.
lcObjective.title: Objective

lcObjectiveGroup.definition: The element <lcObjectiveGroup> provides contains a list of one or more learning objectives.
lcObjectiveGroup.title: Objective group

lcObjectives.definition: The element <lcObjectives> lists or describes the learning goals.
lcObjectives.title: Objectives

lcObjectivesStem.definition: The element <lcObjectivesStem> provides a leading sentence to introduce a list of learning objectives.
lcObjectivesStem.title: Objectives stem

lcOJT.definition: The element <lcOJT> describes technical aspects of the course taking place in the work environment.
lcOJT.title: On The Job Training

lcOrganizational.definition: The element <lcOrganizational> is the first wrapper within <lcNeedsAnalysis>. It describes the organization’s learning requirements.
lcOrganizational.title: Organizational

lcOrgConstraints.definition: The element <lcOrgConstraints> describes organizational aspects that may limit the organization’s ability to effectively use the instruction to meet its goals.
lcOrgConstraints.title: Organizational Constraints

lcPlanAudience.definition: The element <lcPlanAudience> is the second wrapper within the element <lcNeedsAnalysis>. It describes the learners’ profile taking the instruction.
lcPlanAudience.title: Audience

lcPlanDescrip.definition: The element <lcPlanDescrip> provides a complete description of the learning plan.
lcPlanDescrip.title: Plan Description

lcPlanObjective.definition: The element <lcPlanObjective> describes actions, behaviors, conditions and standards required of the learner in order to complete a course.
lcPlanObjective.title: Learning Plan Objective

lcPlanPreReqs.definition: The element <lcPlanPreReqs> provides the knowledge, skills, abilities, courses and other activities learners must have satisfied to take the instruction.
lcPlanPreReqs.title: Plan Prerequisites

lcPlanResources.definition: The element <lcPlanResources> describes the materials available to learners for learning in the course of their daily routine. It may include computers, books, manuals, tutors.
lcPlanResources.title: Plan Resources

lcPlanSubject.definition: The element <lcPlanSubject> provides a complete description of the subject of the planned learning.
lcPlanSubject.title: Subject

lcPlanTitle.definition: The element <lcPlanTitle> provides a title for the lesson plan.
lcPlanTitle.title: Plan Title

lcPlayers.definition: The element <lcPlayers> describes tools used for time-sequenced display at runtime.
lcPlayers.title: Players

lcProcesses.definition: The element <lcProcesses> describes processes learners routinely follow – ISO, SOPs, etc.
lcProcesses.title: Processes

lcProject.definition: The element <lcProject> is the first high level container element in the element <learningPlan>. It contains the learning content project plan description.
lcProject.title: Project

lcQuestion.definition: The <lcQuestion> element is used to hold a question in an assessment interaction.
lcQuestion.title: Question

lcResolution.definition: The element <lcResolution> describes the required computer screen resolution delivered instruction.
lcResolution.title: Resolution

lcResources.definition: The element <lcResources> provides a list of related resources and information about them, such as related articles or samples on the web.
lcResources.title: Resources

lcReview.definition: The element <lcReview> provides a review of the main points.
lcReview.title: Review

lcSection.definition: The element <lcSection> provides a generic element to contain other learning content.
lcSection.title: Section

lcSecurity.definition: The element <lcSecurity> describes the security requirements in the delivered instruction.
lcSecurity.title: Security

lcSequence.definition: The <lcSequence> element provides the position of a sequence option in a sequence in an assessment interaction.
lcSequence.title: Sequence

lcSequenceOption.definition: This element contains the contents of an item to be sequenced within an assessment interaction.
lcSequenceOption.title: Sequence option

lcSequenceOptionGroup.definition: The element <lcSequenceOptionGroup> provides the options for an assessment sequence interaction.
lcSequenceOptionGroup.title: Sequence option group

lcSequencing.definition: The sequence interaction presents the assessment taker with a list of items that must be put into a correct sequential order.
lcSequencing.title: Sequencing

lcSingleSelect.definition: A single select interaction presents the assessment taker with a question and three or more possible answers, only one of which is correct.
lcSingleSelect.title: Single select

lcSkills.definition: The element <lcSkills> describes the learners’ current skill set and the relevancy to the learning plan.
lcSkills.title: Skills

lcSpecChars.definition: The element <lcSpecChars> describes learner characteristics specific to the population that will influence the design, including learning disabilities, physical handicaps, and so forth.
lcSpecChars.title: Special Characteristics

lcSummary.definition: The element <lcSummary> provides a textual summary that describes the main learning goals and lessons learned.
lcSummary.title: Summary

lcTask.definition: The element <lcTask> is the fourth wrapper within the element <lcNeedsAnalysis>. It captures a work item to be performed.
lcTask.title: Task

lcTaskItem.definition: The element <lcTaskItem> is a repeatable wrapper describing discrete tasks to be taught.
lcTaskItem.title: Task Item

lcTechnical.definition: The element <lcTechnical> is the fifth high level container element under the element <learningPlan>. It describes the technical requirements to the learning content and how those requirements are supported by the instructional design.
lcTechnical.title: Technical

lcTime.definition: The element <lcTime> specifies the time expected to complete an activity.
lcTime.title: Time

lcTrueFalse.definition: The true-false interaction presents the learner with two choices: one correct, the other incorrect, and is often presented as true/false or yes/no responses.
lcTrueFalse.title: True-false

lcValues.definition: The element <lcValues> describes affective components of desired instructional outcomes.
lcValues.title: Values

lcViewers.definition: The element <lcViewers> describes viewers used for time-sequenced display at runtime.
lcViewers.title: Viewers

lcW3C.definition: The element <lcW3C> describes standards used for data accessibility and conformity to standards.
lcW3C.title: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)

lcWorkEnv.definition: The element <lcWorkEnv> is the third wrapper tag within the element <lcNeedsAnalysis>. It describes the working conditions and contexts in which the training will be applied.
lcWorkEnv.title: Work Environment

lcWorkEnvDescription.definition: The element <lcWorkEnvDescription> describes the general working environment in which the training will be applied.
lcWorkEnvDescription.title: Work Environment Description

learning.definition: This element is used to contain the five learning information types:
learning.title: Learning content

learningAssessment.definition: A Learning Assessment presents questions or interactions that measure progress, encourage recollection, and stimulate reinforcement of the learning content, and can be presented before the content as a pre-assessment or as a post-assessment test. The format of each interactive assessment question can be structured as one of the following question types: true-false, single select, multiple select, sequencing, matching or hotspot. Therefore, one "learning assessment" can contain a series of individual "interactions", each of which contains a "question type". The interactions use a subset of the Question-Test Interoperability (IMS QTI) specification.
learningAssessment.title: Learning assessment

learningContent.definition: A learning content topic comprises a set of self-contained content about a single terminal learning objective supported by zero or more enabling learning objectives. It provides the learning content itself, and enables direct use of content from the S1000D descript data module. It supports specific objectives declared in the Learning plan topic type.
learningContent.title: Learning content

learningOverview.definition: The learning overview structure covers introductory course information. It identifies the learning objectives, includes other information helpful to the learner, such as prerequisites, duration, intended audience, and can include information and strategies that seek to gain attention and stimulate recall of prior learning.
learningOverview.title: Learning overview content

learningPlan.definition: A learning plan topic describes learning needs and goals, instructional design models, task analyses, learning taxonomies, and other information necessary to the lesson planning process. The learning plan structure is contained within the element <learning>.
learningPlan.title: Learning plan content

learningSummary.definition: A learning summary recaps and provides context for the achievement or accomplishment of learning objectives, provides guidance to reinforce learning and long-term memory, and can pose questions to enhance encoding and verification of the learning content.
learningSummary.title: Learning summary content

legend.definition: The element <legend> contains the legend or explanatory list.
legend.title: Legend

length.definition: The length information element <length> contains the length of a wire. It is recommended to specify in the length type attribute wireLengthType, whether the length information gives the design length, the real length of the wire or a critical length.
length.title: Length information

levelledPara.definition: The element <levelledPara> is the equivalent of a headed paragraph and subparagraphs. It can have one or more <levelledPara> elements nested within it. The depth of this structure is unlimited, however, it is recommended to not exceed five levels of depth. It is further recommended that additional levels only be used in a conversion effort, where existing data is authored to such a depth and restructuring of data is not feasible. In these cases, the structure must never exceed eight levels of depth. The project or the organization must decide on the depth of breakdown.The Schema allows for a single occurrence of <levelledPara> under a parent <levelledPara>. The project or organization must decide whether to allow this structure in their descriptive data modules or to insist on a minimum occurrence of two <levelledPara> elements.
levelledPara.title: Levelled paragraphs

limit.definition: The element <limit> gives the information required to determine when a task must be performed.
limit.title: Limit information

limitRange.definition: The element <limitRange> provides the means to establish that the inspection must be performed between two values.
limitRange.title: Limit range

limitRangeFrom.definition: The element <limitRangeFrom> provides the means to establish the starting limit for a limit range between which the inspection must be performed.
limitRangeFrom.title: Limit range start

limitRangeTo.definition: The element <limitRangeTo> provides the means to establish the ending limit for a limit range between which the inspection must be performed.
limitRangeTo.title: Limit range end

limitType.definition: The element <limitType> is used to express the threshold values and units of the time limit.
limitType.title: Limit type

listItem.definition: This element <listItem> is used to contain the list items themselves. It can contain text, or notes and paragraphs.
listItem.title: List items

listItemDefinition.definition: The element <listItemDefinition> contains the term to be defined. It can contain text, or one or more paragraphs.
listItemDefinition.title: List item definition

listItemTerm.definition: This element is used to contain the term to be defined.
listItemTerm.title: List item term

listOfChoices.definition: The element <listOfChoices> contains a selection of multiple (one or more) choices. Each of these is giving a reference to another action, to the final action (in element <isolationProcedureEnd>) or to close-up requirements (element <closeRqmts>).
listOfChoices.title: Answers - Selection of choice

localFabricationMaterial.definition: This element allows specifying one or several raw part(s) from which the defined part can be manufactured and their dimensions or quantity.
localFabricationMaterial.title: Raw parts

locateAndRepair.definition: The element <locateAndRepair>/<locateAndRepairLruItem> contains any locating and repairing tasks and information on the faulty LRU.
locateAndRepair.title: Locate and repair/Locate and repair LRU

locateAndRepairSruItem.definition: The element <locateAndRepairSruItem> contains any locating and repairing tasks and information on the faulty SRU.
locateAndRepairSruItem.title: Locate and repair SRU

location.definition: This element is used to specify in which zone and/or optionally on which electric panel with coordinates if necessary, the functional item is located.
location.title: Functional item location

locationRcmd.definition: The element <locationRcmd > provides information for each location recommendation
locationRcmd.title: Location recommendation

locationRcmdSegment.definition: The element <locationRcmdSegment> is used to identify an S2000M location recommendation segment (CES). As specified above, this element is only mandatory for S2000M programs.
locationRcmdSegment.title: CES data

logo.definition: The element <logo> contains the reference to the manufacturer’s, project’s or sponsor’s logotype.
logo.title: Logo

lom.definition: The IEEE LOM is a part of the SCO reference model (SCORM) specification. It defines a set of metadata elements for describing learning content, including element names, definitions, data types, and field lengths. The inclusion of the LOM in the SCORM content package allows learning content developers to add metadata about the learning content references within the SCORM content package.
lom.title: Learning Object Model

lowestAuthorizedLevel.definition: The element <lowestAuthorizedLevel> indicates the minimum skill authorized to remove, replace, or use an item. The use of this element will facilitate supplying the bench stock applicable to the maintainer’s skill level without having to go through an entire manual to determine what consumable supplies might be needed. It also alerts the clerk in the supply room of which supplies the maintainer is allowed to acquire for bench stock.
lowestAuthorizedLevel.title: Lowest authorized maintenance level

lowestAuthorizedLevelGroup.definition: The element <lowestAuthorizedLevelGroup> contains groups the different lowest authorized maintenance levels associated to the supply.
lowestAuthorizedLevelGroup.title: Lowest authorized maintenance level group

lru.definition: The element <lru> contains name, a shortname and identification of the LRU.
lru.title: LRU identification

lruItem.definition: The element <lruItem > contains the information needed to perform the test on the faulty LRU.
lruItem.title: Fault isolation test - LRU

mainProcedure.definition: The element <mainProcedure> contains the detailed procedural steps to be done, properly supported by figures, multimedia, foldouts and tables.
mainProcedure.title: Main procedure

maintAllocation.definition: The element <maintAllocation> contains information about maintenance allocations. Maintenance allocations capture maintenance functions along with maintenance levels and time associated for each task. It is contained in the element <maintPlanning> (refer to Para 2.2).
maintAllocation.title: Maintenance allocation

maintAllocationGroup.definition: The element <maintAllocationGroup> is used to group maintenance functional items together.
maintAllocationGroup.title: Maintenance allocation group

maintLevel.definition: The maintenance level is specified by selecting an enumerated value for the attribute maintLevelCode. The estimated work time can be entered as a data string within the element.
maintLevel.title: Maintenance level

maintLevelGroup.definition: This element is used to gather the information about the lowest authorized maintenance level and the associated estimated work time to perform the maintenance. <maintLevel>.
maintLevelGroup.title: Maintenance level group

maintPlanning.definition: Maintenance planning information is captured using the Content section of the four types of maintenance schedule data modules. These four types are time limits, which captures information about periodicities and life details for a system; task definitions, which captures the information about individual tasks to be carried out on a system, inspection definitions, which captures groups of maintenance tasks or inspection types, and maintenance allocation, which captures maintenance functions along with maintenance levels and time associated for each task.
maintPlanning.title: Maintenance planning

maintQualifier.definition: The element <maintQualifier> is used to capture maintenance action qualification such as maintenance function, maintenance level estimated work time, any tools and/or test equipment and any remarks.
maintQualifier.title: Maintenance qualifier

manufacturerCode.definition: The element <manufacturerCode> contains the manufacturer's code.
manufacturerCode.title: Manufacturer code

mass.definition: The element <mass> contains the mass of a connector.
mass.title: Mass

material.definition: The element <material> describes the material of which the  part is made.
material.title: Material

maxDiameter.definition: The element <maxDiameter> gives the maximum diameter of a solder sleeve.
maxDiameter.title: Maximum sleeve diameter

maxHarnessSize.definition: The element <maxHarnessSize> gives the maximum harness size.
maxHarnessSize.title: Maximum harness size

maxMountingPositions.definition: The maximum number of mounting positions element <maxMountingPositions> contains the number of mounting positions on a next higher assembly, eg a circuit breaker panel. This element is only used for equipment that has mounting positions for other electrical equipment, eg connectors or circuit breakers.
maxMountingPositions.title: Maximum number of mounting positions

menu.definition: Menus are the most popular way of getting information from a user. The process data module dialog menu has some powerful features.
menu.title: User menus

menuChoice.definition: The element <menuChoice> represents one possible answer to the prompt question. The text of the answer is marked up by element <prompt>.
menuChoice.title: User choices

message.definition: The element <message> provides information from the IETP to the user or additional instructions or details about a parent dialog.
message.title: User message

messageAlt.definition: The element <messageAlt> contains alternative messages one or none of which are applicable in a given situation and will be displayed to the user. Refer to Para 2.3.4.2.
messageAlt.title: Alternate message

middleName.definition: The element <middleName> contains the middle name of the individual contact.
middleName.title: Middle name

minDiameter.definition: The element <minDiameter> gives the minimum diameter of a solder sleeve.
minDiameter.title: Minimum sleeve diameter

minHarnessSize.definition: The element <minHarnessSize> gives the minimum harness size.
minHarnessSize.title: Minimum harness size

minTemperature.definition: The elements <minTemperature> and <maxTemperature> give the lower and upper temperature rating boundaries for a harness.
minTemperature.title: Harness temperature rating child elements

modelVersion.definition: The element <modelVersion> is used to identify the specific version of the equipment to which the item is fitted in this location.
modelVersion.title: Model version

modification.definition: The element <modification> contains the identification of the retrofit order.
modification.title: Modification

modificationTitle.definition: The element <modificationTitle> contains the title of the modification.
modificationTitle.title: Modification title

multimedia.definition: The element <multimedia> is an optional, repeatable element, used for marking up all multimedia content. It is the parent element of multimedia objects
multimedia.title: Multimedia

multimediaObject.definition: The element <multimediaObject> is an optional, repeatable element, used for marking up multimedia objects.
multimediaObject.title: Multimedia Object

name.definition: The element <name> contains the textual name of the function, circuit breaker, controls and indicators, zone or access point, equipment, product etc.
name.title: Name

natoStockNumber.definition: The element <natoStockNumber> contains the NATO Stock Number (NSN) of the support equipment. Optionally, the complete NSN can be broken into its constituent parts by using its attributes.
natoStockNumber.title: NATO stock number - NSN

networkAnalysisCode.definition: The network analysis code describes the behavior of the wire end in the network connection analysis in relation to other wires via the equipment. It is based on the behavior of the equipment to which the wire end is connected. This element can be used as the basis for the analysis of electrical connections in a system.
networkAnalysisCode.title: Network analysis code

nextHigherAssy.definition: For wires that are part of a physical or logical assembly, eg a box and/or a panel, the next higher assembly element <nextHigherAssy> can be used to identify this equipment.
nextHigherAssy.title: Next higher assembly

noConds.definition: The element <noConds> contains the "marker" for no required actions/conditions. If there are no required actions/conditions for the Procedure then the element <noConds> must be used.
noConds.title: No conditions

notationName.definition: The element <notationName> contains a specific notation name. Each notation, for which special project rules are given, must be specified and its intended use explained.
notationName.title: Notation name

notationRule.definition: The element <notationRule> contains a notation more specific than defined by S1000D. The rule that applies must be specified. An example would be when a project or an organization decides to exclude use of a particular notation.
notationRule.title: Notation specific rule

notationRuleList.definition: The element <notationRuleList> contains excluded notations. A project or an organization can decide to exclude one or several of the notations allowable by S1000D. These restrictions are to be included in the BREX data module.
notationRuleList.title: Notation rules

note.definition: The element <note> contains additional information that can be useful to the user.
note.title: Notes

notePara.definition: The element <notePara> contains the note text.
notePara.title: Note para

notIllustrated.definition: The element <notIllustrated> is used to indicate that an item has not been illustrated. If an item has not been illustrated this element is populated with a hyphen "-".
notIllustrated.title: Not illustrated

numberOfCores.definition: The element <numberOfCores> contains the number of cores of the wire material.
numberOfCores.title: Core

objectPath.definition: The element <objectPath> contains an XPath address defining where the element or attribute occurs in the Schema structure. This must be identified for an element or attribute for which rules are given.
objectPath.title: Object path

objectUse.definition: The element <objectUse> contains a specific description and intended use for each element, attribute, or notation that is recorded in the BREX data module.
objectUse.title: Object use

objectValue.definition: The element <objectValue> contains the description of the intended meaning.
objectValue.title: Object value

observedFault.definition: he element <observedFault> contains information on observed faults but not detected by the computerized maintenance system.
observedFault.title: Observed faults

optionalPart.definition: This element provides one or several optional part(s), ie parts that are strictly equivalent to the defined part.
optionalPart.title: Optional part

optionalSupplierCode.definition: This element contains the CAGE/CAGE code of an additional optional supplier for the part.
optionalSupplierCode.title: Optional supplier code

orientation.definition: The element <orientation> contains orientation/polarization information about a connector. Polarization information is normally given as part of the connector's part number. The polarization code can represent the angle between the main keyway and the other keyways of the connector.
orientation.title: Orientation

originator.definition: The element <originator> contains the identifier of the originating company or organization responsible for the production of the data module/ publication module. The originator’s code is indicated with the company name, the CAGE code, which is the preferred method, or both. Normally, the originator is defined as the designated design authority of the Product; however, projects must nominate the originators. If a responsible partner company has an enterprise code, then that code must be used.
originator.title: Originator

otherItems.definition: This element describes textually which items can be reached from the access point.
otherItems.title: Other items

outerDiameter.definition: The element <outerDiameter> contains the outer diameter information of wire material.
outerDiameter.title: Outer diameter

outerJacketColor.definition: The element <outerJacketColor> contains the color information of the outer jacket of wire material.
outerJacketColor.title: Outer jacket color

overLengthPartNumber.definition: This element contains the initial over length part number for projects, whose part numbers cannot exceed a given length. In this case, the over length part numbers are shortened and the shortened part number is used all over the documentation.
overLengthPartNumber.title: Over length part number

packaging.definition: The element <packaging> contains information about the packaging of the supply.
packaging.title: Packaging

paraBasic.definition: Element <paraBasic> contains a description of the external application or other information that will be displayed to the user.
paraBasic.title: Element <paraBasic>

parameter.definition: The element <parameter> is an optional, repeatable element, which has attributes used for passing parameters to objects within the multimedia scene.
parameter.title: Parameter

partAndSerialNumber.definition: The element <partAndSerialNumber> contains parts and serial numbers.
partAndSerialNumber.title: Part and serial number

partIdent.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, this element identifies semantically the part as a result of its attributes.
partIdent.title: Part identifier

partIdentSegment.definition: The element <partIdentSegment> is used to identify a S2000M Part Identity Segment (PAS). This element is optional to allow the use of external reference to the parts information data of the technical information repository data module.
partIdentSegment.title: PAS data

partKeyword.definition: This element contains the single word name of the part, as defined for the civil aviation.
partKeyword.title: Part keyword

partLocationSegment.definition: The element <partLocationSegment> is used to identify a S2000M Part Location Data Segment (CBS).
partLocationSegment.title: Part location data

partRef.definition: This element is used to markup a part (outside of its specification in the part technical repository) and also allows referring to its position in the part technical repository.
partRef.title: Part

partRefGroup.definition: This element contains the different types of relationships with other parts.
partRefGroup.title: Relationships with other parts

partRepository.definition: This element is used to provide a list of parts and their associated properties.
partRepository.title: General

partSpec.definition: This element represents a part. It contains its associated properties.
partSpec.title: Part specification

person.definition: The element <person> contains the skill information on the required personnel for the task when there are requirements to individually specify the personnel.
person.title: Person

personCategory.definition: The element <personCategory> contains the required category level of the person.
personCategory.title: Category

personnel.definition: The element <personnel> contains the information on the required personnel for the task by grouping the personnel by category, skill level and trade/trade code together with the number of personnel of a certain skill (category, skill level, trade).
personnel.title: Personnel

personSkill.definition: The element <personSkill> contains the required skill level of the person. This represents the skill level that the person must have attained to be able to perform his or her role in the Procedure and is, eg Basic, Intermediate or Advanced.
personSkill.title: Skill level

phoneNumber.definition: The element <phoneNumber> is repeatable and contains contact phone numbers for the business.
phoneNumber.title: Phone numbers

physicalSecurityPilferageCode.definition: The element <physicalSecurityPilferageCode> is used to indicate the degree of security or pilferage risk associated with the item.
physicalSecurityPilferageCode.title: Physical security/pilferage code

pm.definition: The element <pm> defines the content and structure of a publication.
pm.title: Publication module

pmAddress.definition: The element <pmAddress> contains the publication module address information.
pmAddress.title: Publication module address

pmAddressItems.definition: The element <pmAddressItems> includes additional information about a publication module.
pmAddressItems.title: Publication module address items

pmCode.definition: The element <pmCode> contains the publication module code. Publication modules produced according to this specification must be given a Publication module code.
pmCode.title: Publication module code

pmEntryTitle.definition: The element <pmEntryTitle> contains the title of the publication entry. The title for the following entries must be given. It can be used for the table of contents.
pmEntryTitle.title: Title of the publication module entry

pmIdent.definition: The element <pmIdent> contains the publication module identification information.
pmIdent.title: Publication module identification

pmRef.definition: The element <pmRef> contains details of the destination publication module that is referred from some other S1000D context, such as a data module, another publication module etc.
pmRef.title: References to publications

pmRefAddressItems.definition: The element <pmRefAddressItems> contains additional identifying information about the destination publication module.
pmRefAddressItems.title: Complementary identifying information for a publication module

pmRefGroup.definition: This element contains one or several references to publication modules to which the comment/response relates.
pmRefGroup.title: Publication module reference group

pmRefIdent.definition: The element <pmRefIdent> contains the items forming a unique identification of the destination data module.
pmRefIdent.title: Identification of a referred publication module

pmStatus.definition: The element <pmStatus> contains the publication module status.
pmStatus.title: Publication module status information

pmTitle.definition: The element <pmTitle> gives the meaning of the publication and is defined by the project.
pmTitle.title: Publication module title

policyStatement.definition: The element <policyStatement> contains the reference to the security policy information.
policyStatement.title: Policy reference

positionOnNextHigherAssy.definition: Equipment, which is mounted on a physical assembly, eg a box or a panel, has allocated the identification of the position on the next higher assembly element <positionOnNextHigherAssy>. The position is indicated either by a direct position or by grid coordinates.
positionOnNextHigherAssy.title: Position on next higher assembly

postalZipCode.definition: The element <postalZipCode> contains the zip code for the business.
postalZipCode.title: Postal zip code

postOfficeBox.definition: The element <postOfficeBox> contains the post office box of the business defined.
postOfficeBox.title: Post office box

potentialConnectionsOrder.definition: This element is used in the situation when more than one wire is connected to an electrical potential, eg an earth bolt. All these wires must have the same value for the electrical potential block grouping information in the wire connection code. In this case, these wires must have ascending numerical values at the potential connections of the wire connection code, which orders the wire to facilitate graphical presentation.
potentialConnectionsOrder.title: Potential connections order

preferredSparePart.definition: This element provides one or several preferred spare part(s), ie parts that are recommended by the data provider.
preferredSparePart.title: Preferred spare parts

preliminaryRqmts.definition: The element <preliminaryRqmts> groups together all information about resources that can be required before the accomplishment of the task.
preliminaryRqmts.title: Preliminary requirements

preparationInfo.definition: For wires, the content model preparationInfo/finishingInfo defines the child elements <preparationInfo> and <finishingInfo>.
preparationInfo.title: Content model preparationInfo/finishingInfo

proceduralStep.definition: The element <proceduralStep > contains a step in the procedure. A step can be broken down into substeps by including another element <proceduralStep>, which can itself be broken down further into substeps by including another element <proceduralStep>, and so on following the lower branch in Fig 1. In this way, any depth of substep breakdown can be achieved. However, it is highly discouraged not to exceed five levels of depth. The substep breakdown must never exceed eight levels of depth (for details, refer to Business rules decisions below).
proceduralStep.title: Procedural step

proceduralStepAlt.definition: The element <proceduralStepAlt> provides the capability to group in one structure several potential steps of data for display. Only one or none will be displayed depending on the applicability assigned to the element <proceduralStep> within the element <proceduralStepAlt>. Refer to Para 2.3.4.2.
proceduralStepAlt.title: Procedural step alternate

procedure.definition: The element <procedure> contains all information necessary to carry out the task or the main objective of the procedural information.
procedure.title: Procedure

process.definition: The element <process> is the top level element containing the process flow constructs.
process.title: Process Flow Constructs

procurementData.definition: This element groups the properties to procure the part.
procurementData.title: Procurement data

product.definition: The element <product> identifies an individual product instance.
product.title: Product

productAttribute.definition: The element <productAttribute> is used to declare a single attribute of the Product, such as "serial number" or "model".
productAttribute.title: Product attribute

productAttributeList.definition: The element <productAttributeList> contains a list of attributes of the Product. The values for product attributes will typically not change throughout the service life of product instance.
productAttributeList.title: Product attributes

productConfiguration.definition: The element <productConfiguration> contains a reference to the Product configuration as defined for production in the authority block. Any deviation from that configuration or standard is shown by inserting the modification number.
productConfiguration.title: Product configuration

productCrossRefTableRef.definition: The element <productCrossRefTableRef> provides a reference to the PCT data module for this project.
productCrossRefTableRef.title: PCT reference

productionMaintData.definition: The element <productionMaintData> contains the basic information required for the planning and preparation of the task.
productionMaintData.title: Production maintenance data

productSafety.definition: The element <productSafety> contains an indication when a module is transmitting information that affects the safety of the product’s users. The element <productSafety> can be empty or can contain textual information describing the urgency for processing the information in the module and handling of the module when third parties now operate the Product.
productSafety.title: Product safety

prompt.definition: The element <prompt> contains text that is the question or information for the user. Refer to Chap 3.9.5.2.1.10.
prompt.title: User prompts

province.definition: The element <province> contains the province where the business is located.
province.title: Province

pubMedia.definition: The repeatable element <pubMedia> specifies the information about how the media on which the publication is delivered.
pubMedia.title: Publication media

pushButton.definition: The element <pushButton> provides a means to supply information for the data field entry(s) thru an external application (eg, diagnostic test, sound, and video) or secondary dialog (eg, advanced features).
pushButton.title: Push button

qualityAssurance.definition: The element <qualityAssurance> contains details of the status of the QA process as required by the project. The data module/ publication module must be identified as either being unverified or verified. This element can contain applicability information to indicate the applicability of the QA information. This applicability information must be a subset of the mandatory applicability settings for the complete data module. This applies equally to the element <qualityAssurance> and all its subelements.
qualityAssurance.title: Quality assurance status

quantity.definition: The element <quantity> provides the capability to identify a portion of a paragraph that corresponds to a numeric value with a special meaning, such as a torque value. The exact meaning of the quantity data can be specified using a set of predefined S1000D values, or extended to support specific project needs.
quantity.title: Quantity data

quantityGroup.definition: The element <quantityGroup> contains a group of values and tolerances and/or multiple values in the case where multiple units of measure are used (eg 2 h 30 min).
quantityGroup.title: Quantity group

quantityPerNextHigherAssy.definition: The element <quantityPerNextHigherAssy> is used to store the Quantity per Next higher Assembly (QNA) of an item. If the item is included for reference only the letters "REF" are entered. If the quantity cannot be established or it is otherwise not appropriate to include the data, the letters "AR" (As Required) are entered.
quantityPerNextHigherAssy.title: Quantity per next higher assembly

quantityTolerance.definition: The element <quantityTolerance> contains a decimal tolerance value, the type of tolerance, and an optional unit of measure. The tolerance value must conform to the W3C XML standard for decimal values which reuires use a period [.] for the separator between the integralpart and the fractionalpart, and no thousands separator. The display format is not specified in the XML code, but must conform to program or country requirements at presentation (refer to Chap 3.9.1 for rules on presentation).
quantityTolerance.title: Tolerance

quantityValue.definition: The element <quantityValue> contains a decimal value and an optional unit of measure. The value must conform to the W3C XML standard for decimal values which requires use a period [.] for the separator between the integral part and the fractional part, and no thousands separator. The display format is not specified in the XML code but, must conform to program or country requirements at presentation (Refer to Chap 3.9.1 for rules on presentation).
quantityValue.title: Value

rack.definition: The element <rack> contains rack information about rack & panel connectors.
rack.title: Rack

randomList.definition: The element <randomList> contains random lists. It can contain applicability information, a title and the list items themselves.
randomList.title: Random list

rcmd.definition: The element <rcmd> contains the recommendations linked to the supply requirement alternative.
rcmd.title: Recommendation

rcmdQuantity.definition: The element <rcmdQuantity> contains the tool recommended quantity.
rcmdQuantity.title: Recommended quantity

reasonForAmendment.definition: If used, the element <reasonForAmendment> must record the reason for amendment of either a complete figure, or of individual illustration sheets of a multi-sheet figure. This is to be used to indicate changes made to the illustration itself, for example, "location view has been added", or "cross-section view has been added for Mod. XYZ".
reasonForAmendment.title: Reason for amendment

reasonForSelection.definition: The element <reasonForSelection> is used to store the Reason For Selection (RFS) of an item.
reasonForSelection.title: Reason for selection

reasonForUpdate.definition: The element <reasonForUpdate> contains a short explanation of the reason for updating of the data module/ publication module. For more details, refer to Chap 3.9.5.2.1.1.
reasonForUpdate.title: Reason for update

receiveByName.definition: Element <receiveByName> is used when the external application returns data in name/value pairs.
receiveByName.title: Receive by name

receiveByPosition.definition: Element <receiveByPosition> is used when the external application returns data in a stream of delimited values by position.
receiveByPosition.title: Receive by position

receiveValue.definition: Element <receiveValue> contains element <variableRef> which is the variable to be assigned the value received from the external application. When the returned values exceed the number of receiveValue definitions, the remaining receiveValue information is discarded.
receiveValue.title: Receive value

referenceDesignator.definition: The reference designator is the unique identifier of electrical equipment in the system.
referenceDesignator.title: Reference designator

referTo.definition: The element <referTo> is used to contain a reference to multiple IPP or CSN.
referTo.title: Refer to

refs.definition: The element <refs> is used to populate the standardized tabular list "Table 1 References". This paragraph gives the rules and recommendations for inclusion of the standardized tabular list "Table 1 References" at the beginning of the data module content section.
refs.title: References presented in the reference table of a data module

relatedTask.definition: The attributes of this element identify another task that has an association to the current task and provide a code that indicates the nature of the association.
relatedTask.title: Related task

remarks.definition: The element <remarks> can contain general remarks. If there are no remarks then this element need not be used.
remarks.title: Remarks

remarksGroup.definition: The element <remarksGroup> is used to capture data about the tool or test equipment. It includes elements for tools list code, maintenance, nomenclature, NSN, and tool number.
remarksGroup.title: Remarks group

remarksList.definition: The element <remarksList> is used to list remarks pertinent to the maintenance functions listed in maintenance allocation data. The purpose is to provide a list for referencing from maintenance allocation. When remarks are indicated in the maintenance allocation, the remarks list must be included.
remarksList.title: Remarks list

remarksRefs.definition: The element <remarksRefs> is used to contain a reference to remarks contained in the remarks list within the maintenance allocation data.
remarksRefs.title: Remarks References

repair.definition: The element <repair> contains any repair procedure.
repair.title: Repair

replacedBy.definition: This element provides a part that can replace the defined part. The kind of replacement is specified by its attribute. It is also possible to associate a textual condition to this replacement relationship. Some replacement relationships can only be applicable to some product instances.
replacedBy.title: Replacement relationship

replacementCond.definition: This element is used to specify the condition that has to be fulfilled for the replacement, if any.
replacementCond.title: Replacement condition

reqCond.definition: The element <reqCond> contains the required action/condition statement, such as "Open the circuit breaker:" or "Make sure the circuit breaker is open, safetied/locked and tagged:" (which might require a separate Procedure).
reqCond.title: Required condition

reqCondCircuitBreaker.definition: The element <reqCondCircuitBreaker> contains a set of circuit breaker actions (open or close)/conditions (open or closed) before the performance of the task.
reqCondCircuitBreaker.title: Required conditions - circuit breaker list

reqCondDm.definition: The element <reqCondDm> contains the required action/condition when satisfied by completing a Procedure that is described in a separate data module.
reqCondDm.title: Required conditions - referenced data module

reqCondExternalPub.definition: The element <reqCondExternalPub> contains the required action/condition when are contained in a non S1000D publication or document.
reqCondExternalPub.title: Required conditions - referenced non S1000D publication or document

reqCondGroup.definition: This element <reqCondGroup> contains any required conditions information. Required conditions are actions to be done and/or conditions that must be satisfied before the Procedure which is the subject of the data module is started.
reqCondGroup.title: Required conditions

reqCondNoRef.definition: The element <reqCondNoRef> contains the action/condition on its own with no referenced data module or technical publication to represent a simple one step action/condition that does not require further explanation.
reqCondNoRef.title: Required condition - simple action/condition

reqCondPm.definition: The element <reqCondPm> contains the required action/condition when they are contained in another publication module.
reqCondPm.title: Required conditions - referenced publication module

reqPersons.definition: The element <reqPersons> contains the information on the required personnel for the task.
reqPersons.title: Required persons

reqQuantity.definition: The element <reqQuantity> contains the number of equipment items that are subject to the time limit in the scope of the Product.
reqQuantity.title: Required quantity

reqSafety.definition: The element <reqSafety> must contain information to list any safety requirements.
reqSafety.title: Required safety

reqSpares.definition: This element <reqSpares> must contain information to list any required spares.
reqSpares.title: Required spares

reqSupplies.definition: The element <reqSupplies> contains information to list any required supplies.
reqSupplies.title: Required supplies

reqSupportEquips.definition: The element <reqSupportEquips> must contain information to list any support equipment including special tools, required to accomplish the Procedure contained in the data module. Common types of test equipment such as voltmeters, signal generators and continuity testers must be listed. Common tools that are part of a standard tool kit must not be listed.
reqSupportEquips.title: Required support equipment

reqTechInfo.definition: The element <reqTechInfo> contains the content of <reqTechInfoGroup>.
reqTechInfo.title: Required technical information

scormContentPackageIdent.definition: The SCORM content package identification contains the code that makes up the address for either a full learning event or a single or collection of learning products. The SCORM content package identification is contained within the markup element <scormContentPackageIdent>.identifies the complete aggregation.
scormContentPackageIdent.title: SCORM content package identification

scormContentPackageMedia.definition: This element has mandatory attributes: type and code (label) of the media on which the SCORM content package is delivered. Additional optional attributes are volume and location of the media. This element can be repeated.
scormContentPackageMedia.title: SCORM content package media

scormContentPackageStatus.definition: The SCORM Content Package Status is used to identify the configuration and life cycle status of the learning content product. Information includes applicability, QA checks, and system breakdown numbers.
scormContentPackageStatus.title: SCORM content package status

scormContentPackageTitle.definition: The SCORM content package address title contains the name of the learning product deliverable.
scormContentPackageTitle.title: SCORM content package title

screen.definition: The element <screen> and its attributes contain information of the type of the wire in a shielding situation and the identification of the screen to which the wire end is connected.
screen.title: Screen/shield information

screenCount.definition: The element <screenCount> contains the number of screens of the wire material.
screenCount.title: Screen count

screenGroup.definition: The list of screens element <screenGroup> is used as a container for the subordinate screen/shield information elements.
screenGroup.title: List of screens

screenOrder.definition: The shielding order element <screenOrder> contains an ascending numerical value, which represents the order of the wires connected to an equipment, for graphical presentation of the shielding situation.
screenOrder.title: Shielding order

secondVerification.definition: The element <secondVerification> contains identifies a data module which has been second verified. Data modules cannot be only second verified. They must also be first verified. For details on verification, refer to Chap 3.7.
secondVerification.title: Second verification

sectionIdent.definition: Wires which are connected by non-functional breaks such as connectors, terminal junction modules, splices, etc, often get the same wire identification number and different section identifications. In this case, the wire section identification element must be populated with the identifiers for these different sections.
sectionIdent.title: Wire section identification

security.definition: The element <security> contains the security classification of the complete data module/ publicatio module and its contained or associated illustrations.
security.title: Security classification

selectOrManufacture.definition: The element <selectOrManufacture> is used to identify the range of items to be used for the selection, manufacture, rework or repair of an item. Items should be identified using the CSN, figure number and item number or just item number as appropriate.
selectOrManufacture.title: Select or manufacture

selectOrManufactureFromIdent.definition: The element <selectOrManufactureFromIdent> is used to indicate that an item must be selected to suit specific operating conditions, or that the item can be locally manufactured.
selectOrManufactureFromIdent.title: Select or manufacture from identifier

send.definition: Element <send> defines parameters to send to the called application.
send.title: Element <send>

sequentialList.definition: The element <sequentialList> contains sequential lists, which are also known as ordered lists. It can contain applicability information, a title and the list items themselves.
sequentialList.title: General

serialNumber.definition: The element <serialNumber> contains the listing of a single serial number or a range.
serialNumber.title: Serial number

service.definition: The element <service> is used to identify the user service to which specific data is applicable. The first two characters of this element should be populated with the user nation code. The third character is project specific.
service.title: Service

shelfLife.definition: The element <shelfLife> contains information about the shelf life of the supply.
shelfLife.title: Shelf life

shippingInfo.definition: The element <shippingInfo> contains the shipping information for the supply if any. They are divided into fours types of information.
shippingInfo.title: Shipping information

shortDescr.definition: The element <shortDescr> gives a description of the element which it is contained in.
shortDescr.title: Short Description

shortPmTitle.definition: The element <shortPmTitle> contains the short title of the publication and is defined by the project.
shortPmTitle.title: Short publication module title

shrinkSleeve.definition: The element <shrinkSleeve> is contained in the list of shrink sleeves element <shrinkSleeveGroup>. The list of shrink sleeves is a child element of the list of the standard parts element <standardPartGroup>.
shrinkSleeve.title: Element <shrinkSleeve> and child elements

shuntGroupingValue.definition: This element is only used for equipment with internal logic. It provides grouping information for contacts that belong to the same shunt/bus of a termination module or the same position of a switch or a relay.
shuntGroupingValue.title: Shunt grouping information

siblingPlugIdent.definition: The element <siblingPlugIdent> contains the reference designator of the mate connector in the subordinate element <referenceDesignator>. That means, the plug gets as twin connector identification the reference designator of the receptacle, and the receptacle gets as twin connector identification the reference designator of the plug.
siblingPlugIdent.title: Twin connector identification

signalInfo.definition: The signal information element <signalInfo> contains information about the signals on a wire. This can be the signal name, the effective voltage, the effective current or the waveform of the signal.
signalInfo.title: Signal information

simplePara.definition: The element <simplePara> contains a minimum set of text subelements. It is used where the full set of elements that are available in a full paragraph (element <para>) are not required. Simple paragraphs are used in eg the element <reasonForUpdate> and the element <remarks>.
simplePara.title: Simple paragraph

simpleRemark.definition: The element <simpleRemark> contains general remarks about the shipping information related to the supply.
simpleRemark.title: General remark

SITA.definition: The element <SITA> contains the address supplied in the aviation industry by SITA.
SITA.title: SITA address

size.definition: The element <size> contains the size information of a shrink sleeve.
size.title: Size

skillLevel.definition: The element <skillLevel> contains identify the skill level to which the data module has been written.
skillLevel.title: Skill level

sleeve.definition: The element <sleeve> gives information about a harness sleeve.
sleeve.title: Harness sleeve information

sleeveDiameter.definition: The element <sleeveDiameter> describes minimum and maximum diameter information for a solder sleeve.
sleeveDiameter.title: Sleeve Diameter

sleeveGroup.definition: diameter information for a solder sleeve.
sleeveGroup.title: List of harness sleeves

snsAssy.definition: The element <snsAssy> contains the specification of each assembly defined for the SNS sub-subsystem concerned.
snsAssy.title: SNS assembly code

snsCode.definition: The element <snsCode> contains a code used to define a component in an SNS structure. The code concerned is represented as text content. Depending on the context it can be either the code of a system, a subsystem, a sub-subsystem or an assembly.
snsCode.title: SNS code

snsDescr.definition: The element <snsDescr> provides a description of each specific SNS system.
snsDescr.title: SNS description

snsRules.definition: The element <snsRules> can provide descriptions of one or several SNS systems that apply to the project concerned.
snsRules.title: SNS rules

snsSubSubsystem.definition: The element <snsSubSubsystem> contains the specification of each sub-subsystem defined for the SNS subsystem concerned.
snsSubSubsystem.title: SNS sub-subsystem code

snsSubSystem.definition: The element <snsSubSystem> contains the specification of each subsystem defined for the SNS system.
snsSubSystem.title: SNS subsystem code

snsSystem.definition: The element <snsSystem>contains the specification of each system defined for the SNS.
snsSystem.title: SNS system code

snsTitle.definition: The element <snsTitle> contains a title corresponding to a code used to define a component in an SNS structure. The title is represented as text content. Depending on the context it can be either the title of a system, a subsystem, a sub-subsystem or an assembly.
snsTitle.title: SNS title

solderSleeve.definition: The element <solderSleeve> is contained in the list of solder sleeves element <solderSleeveGroup>. The list of solder sleeves is a child element of the list of the standard parts element <standardPartGroup>.
solderSleeve.title: Description of element <solderSleeve> and child elements

sourceDmIdent.definition: The element <sourceDmIdent> contains the identification of the source data module on which the current data module instance is based.
sourceDmIdent.title: Source data module identification part

sourceMaintRecoverability.definition: The element <sourceMaintRecoverability> is used to identify maintenance activities which are performed on an item. The population of this element is in accordance with Table 7.
sourceMaintRecoverability.title: Source maintenance and recoverability

sourcePmIdent.definition: The element <sourcePmIdent> contains the source publication module identification information such as publication module code, language and issue information.
sourcePmIdent.title: Source publication module identification

sourceScoIdent.definition: The element <sourceScoIdent> contains the identification of the source SCO.
sourceScoIdent.title: Source SCO identification

sourceType.definition: This element <sourceType> provides a means to classify the source of the requirement.
sourceType.title: Source type
