spanspec.definition: The element <spanspec> (span specification) identifies a horizontal span of columns and associated attributes that can subsequently be referenced by its spanname for repeated use in a table’s <entry> elements. A <spanspec> uses column names from <colspec>s defined in that context. It gets default values from the <colspec> that provides the namest. namest and nameend identify the first and last columns in increasing left-to-right order that identify the span. The reason colname is used rather than colnum in identifying <spanspec> is that the names are independent of revisions that can change the number of inserted/deleted columns, as long as namest remains to the left of (has a smaller colnum than) nameend. In a <thead> or <tfoot>, if any <colspec>s are redefined, the <tgroup> <spanspec>s are ignored in references to spanname from <entry>s within this <thead> or <tfoot>. When such redefinition occurs, any spanning should be by namest and nameend.
spanspec.title: Span specification

sparePartClass.definition: This element is used to contain the spare part class code, through its attribute.
sparePartClass.title: Spare part class code

specDocument.definition: This element is used to identify specifications of the part (drawing number for manufacturer parts, standard specification number for standard parts).
specDocument.title: Specification

specialConnection.definition: Description: This element is used to identify specifications of the part (drawing number for
specialConnection.title: Special connections

specialStorage.definition: manufacturer parts, standard specification number for standard parts).
specialStorage.title: Special storage

specificationGroup.definition: The element <specificationGroup> lists the specification that the supply meets.
specificationGroup.title: Specification list

sru.definition: The element <sru> contains name, a shortname and identification of the SRU.
sru.title: SRU identification

sruItem.definition: The element <sruItem> contains the information needed to perform the test on the faulty SRU.
sruItem.title: Fault isolation test - SRU

state.definition: The element <state> contains the state where the business is located.
state.title: State

stockNumber.definition: This element is used to store the number assigned by the customer to identify and control the part in their inventory and control system. As this value depends on the customer, the attribute applicRefId and the referenced element <applic>, which must be populated in accordance with Chap 3.9.5.3, allows specifying the customer.
stockNumber.title: Customer or stock part number

street.definition: The element <street> contains the street address of the business.
street.title: Street

structureObjectRule.definition: The element <structureObjectRule> contains rules that apply to an element or an attribute, which must be given when the intended use of that object does not fully coincide with the specification, for instance by being more restrictive.
structureObjectRule.title: Structure object rule

structureObjectRuleGroup.definition: The element <structureObjectRuleGroup> specifies all rules about the project-specific use of elements and attributes for all the various document types (Schema) used within the project.
structureObjectRuleGroup.title: Structure rules

subCrewDrill.definition: The element <subCrewDrill> is used to identify a subdrill, which is part of a crew/operator drill.
subCrewDrill.title: Subdrill statement

subjectIdent.definition: The element <subjectIdent> is used to store the subject's identification (SID) and provides identification of the item, or items, which are the subjects of the IPPN.
subjectIdent.title: Subject identification

subjectVariantSegment.definition: the element <subjectVariantSegment> is used to identify the S2000M subject variant segment (VAS). It is used as an extension of the IPPN to store information regarding the identification (PN, NSCM and NSN) of the subject for which the IPP has been prepared. In those cases where the IPP presents data against variants of the subject, then this element is repeated the appropriate number of times to hold all the variants' identifications (limited to eight as stated in S2000M).
subjectVariantSegment.title: Subject variant

subScript.definition: The element <subScript> contains the text that is intended to be presented subscripted.
subScript.title: Subscript

superScript.definition: The element <superScript> contains the text that is intended to be presented superscripted.
superScript.title: Superscript

supersedure.definition: The element <supersedure> contains a notice that the data module supersedes other data modules.
supersedure.title: Supersedure

supervisorLevel.definition: The element <supervisorLevel> contains the hierarchical level in the supervisory structure that explain if the supervisor must observe the task or inspect the results of the task.
supervisorLevel.title: Supervisor level

suppliedBy.definition: The element <suppliedBy> is used to contain information about a supplier of the supply.
suppliedBy.title: Supplier

supplierCode.definition: This element contains the CAGE code of the authorized prime source supplier for the part.
supplierCode.title: Supplier code

supplierGroup.definition: The element <supplierGroup> is used to specify the supply product list of suppliers.
supplierGroup.title: Supplier list

supplyIdent.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, the element <supplyIdent> identifies semantically the supply as a result of its attributes.
supplyIdent.title: Supply identifier

supplyRef.definition: The element <supplyRef> represents a supply and also allows referring to its definition in the supply technical repository.
supplyRef.title: Supply

supplyRepository.definition: The element <supplyRepository> is used to provide a list of supplies and their associated properties.
supplyRepository.title: General

supplyRqmtAlt.definition: The element <supplyRqmtAlt> represents one alternative of the supply requirement. Each alternative lists one or several supplies that fulfill the supply requirement.
supplyRqmtAlt.title: Alternatives of the supply requirement

supplyRqmtAltIdent.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, the element <supplyRqmtAltIdent> identifies semantically the supply requirement as a result of its attributes.
supplyRqmtAltIdent.title: Alternate supply item identifier

supplyRqmtIdent.definition: Contrary to the attribute id, the element <supplyRqmtIdent> identifies semantically the supply requirement as a result of its attributes.
supplyRqmtIdent.title: Supply requirement identifier

supplyRqmtRef.definition: The element <supplyRqmtRef> contains the reference to a consumable, material and expendable for projects which manage a technical information repository.
supplyRqmtRef.title: Supply requirement reference

supplyRqmtRepository.definition: The element <supplyRqmtRepository> is used to provide a list of supply requirements and their associated properties.
supplyRqmtRepository.title: General

supplyRqmtSpec.definition: The element <supplyRqmtSpec> represents one supply requirement. It contains its associated properties.
supplyRqmtSpec.title: Supply requirement specification

supplySet.definition: The element <supplySet> identifies supplies that have to be used together (eg base and primer supply).
supplySet.title: Supply set

supplySetGroup.definition: The element <supplySetGroup> is constituted of supplies and/or sets of supplies. Each supply or set of supplies can be used equally.
supplySetGroup.title: Supplies

supplySpec.definition: The element <supplySpec> represents a supply. It contains its associated properties.
supplySpec.title: Supply specification

supportEquipDescr.definition: The element <supportEquipDescr> contains the information on each item of support equipment.
supportEquipDescr.title: Support equipment description

surfaceProtection.definition: The element <surfaceProtection> contains the protection information applied to the surface of a distribution part.
surfaceProtection.title: Protection

symbol.definition: The element <symbol> contains illustrations and graphics that are intended to be presented inline within the normal text. Symbols must be controlled using the ICN, as described in Chap 4.4. However, the ICN must not be presented.
symbol.title: Symbol

systemBreakdownCode.definition: The element <systemBreakdownCode> contains a code that captures the physical breakdown for those projects that are producing data modules that are inline with other logistic databases.
systemBreakdownCode.title: System breakdown code

table.definition: The element <table> is used to contain information which is to be presented in a tabular form. The element is used for both formal and informal tables.
table.title: Table markup

task.definition: The element <task> has general data for a task that belongs to an inspection.
task.title: Task

taskCategory.definition: The element <taskCategory> is used to specify the usage of the tool (eg servicing, maintenance, overhaul, repair etc). This is done through its attribute.
taskCategory.title: Task code

taskDefinition.definition: The element <taskDefinition> contains the task information necessary to schedule maintenance.
taskDefinition.title: Task definition

taskDuration.definition: The element <taskDuration> contains the (one) elapsed time necessary to achieve the maintenance action.
taskDuration.title: Maintenance task duration

taskGroup.definition: The element <taskGroup> represents a list of tasks that belong to the inspection. This element facilitates production of a table of tasks in an inspection.
taskGroup.title: Task group

taskItem.definition: The element <taskItem> represents an individual task that belongs to an inspection.
taskItem.title: Task item

tbody.definition: The element <tbody> (table body) contains the rows of the table that provide the primary content and is mandatory for all tables. The table body must contain at least one table row.
tbody.title: Table body

techData.definition: This element groups the technical properties related to the part.
techData.title: Technical data

techName.definition: The element <techName> content must reflect the name of the hardware or function. That is, it must reflect the system, subsystem or sub-subsystem concerned.
techName.title: Technical name

techPubBase.definition: The element <techPubBase> contains the technical publication baseline to which the data module is written. The publication baseline number represents the technical build standard, of the Product, which defines the technical standard by reference to a certain point in time. This is achieved by declaring a "Cut–off date" or milestone and listing the drawing set standard, relevant modification documents, etc, issued prior to the Cut–off or milestone date and used as source material for the production of data modules. The technical standard so defined, ensures that all data modules are to the same standard. Projects can also decide to use this element to record the delivery number of the Logistics Support Analysis Record (LSAR) to which the data module is written.
techPubBase.title: Publication baseline number

techRepository.definition: This element is used to contain one type of technical information repository to be chosen among the list of technical information repository types.
techRepository.title: Technical repository

techStandard.definition: The element <techStandard> contains the authorized technical standard and associated data to be entered, describing the information basis used to write the data module. The information basis can be described by giving, for example, the modification or drawing standard including amendments, alterations etc or a publication baseline. Technical standard, in this context, is defined as the technical design and development level of the technical information of the Product, on which the data module has been based. This element contains authority block or technical publications baseline number or both.
techStandard.title: Technical standard

temperature.definition: The element <temperature> describes the approved  minimum and maximum temperature rating, for which the harness is approved.
temperature.title: Temperature

terminationModuleGroupingValue.definition: This element is only used for equipment with internal logic. It provides grouping information for contacts that belong to the same module of a termination module assembly.
terminationModuleGroupingValue.title: Termination module grouping information

termTitle.definition: The element <termTitle> contains the column title for the term.
termTitle.title: Term title

testParameters.definition: The element <testParameters> contains a set of attributes to capture parameters for the test.
testParameters.title: Test parameters

tfoot.definition: The element <tfoot> (table footer) contains the rows and entries that represent the table footer. The table footer is to appear at the end of the table (ie after the last table body row). For page-oriented publications, the table footer is to appear after the last row of each page on which the table appears.
tfoot.title: Table footer

tgroup.definition: A table can contain one or more table group <tgroup> elements. Normally, there will be one table group. Multiple table groups are used to define portions of the table that have different presentation requirements (eg column and row specifications).
tgroup.title: Table group

thead.definition: The element <thead> (table header) contains the rows of the table that provide the column headings and is mandatory for S1000D formal tables. The table header is displayed in bold type face and, for page-oriented output, will be displayed at the top of each page on which the table appears. The table header must contain at least one table row. There is no need to use emphasis to make a table header bold.
thead.title: Table header

thermoCoupleMinus.definition: The element <thermoCoupleMinus> identifies the negative contact of thermo couples.
thermoCoupleMinus.title: Thermo couple minus

thermoCouplePlus.definition: The element <thermoCouplePlus> identifies the positive contact of thermo couples.
thermoCouplePlus.title: Thermo couple plus

threshold.definition: The element <threshold> provides the ability to describe limit information in terms of a value before which the inspection must be performed. The value can be given in calendar time or in other terms such as the number of hours a Product has been operating.
threshold.title: Threshold information

thresholdInterval.definition: The element <thresholdInterval> contains any (one or more) threshold interval information that is relevant to the task. It is populated in the format of threshold or threshold interval value, eg 25 (followed by the value of the attribute unitOfMeasure, eg FH).
thresholdInterval.title: Threshold interval

thumbTabText.definition: The element <thumbTabText> is used to contain thumb tab text for the drill or subdrill.
thumbTabText.title: Tab text

timeLimit.definition: The element <timeLimit> is used to express the time limits.
timeLimit.title: Time limit

timeLimitCategory.definition: The element <timeLimitCategory> is used to classify the time limit.
timeLimitCategory.title: Time limit category

timeLimitInfo.definition: The element <timeLimitInfo> is used to contain time limit, periodicities and life details information relating to equipments or systems.
timeLimitInfo.title: Time limit information

title.definition: The element <title> contains the title for a paragraph, step, table or figure, etc.
title.title: Title

tolerance.definition: The element <tolerance> allows the threshold to be given as minimum and maximum value between which the inspection must be performed. The minimum value is determined by subtracting the value of toleranceLow from the value of the threshold. The maximum value is determined by adding the value of toleranceHigh to the value of the threshold.
tolerance.title: Tolerance information

toolAlt.definition: The element <toolAlt> contains the properties of the tool that depend on the Product configuration. Thus this element contains applicability.
toolAlt.title: Alternate tool

toolIdent.definition: Contrarily to the id attribute, the element <toolIdent> identifies semantically the tool thanks to its attributes.
toolIdent.title: Tool identifier

toolRef.definition: The element <toolRef> contains the reference to a tool, for those projects which manage a technical information repository.
toolRef.title: Tool reference

toolRefGroup.definition: The element <toolRefGroup> allows providing relationships and the type of relationship with other tools.
toolRefGroup.title: Relationships with others tools

toolRepository.definition: The element <toolRepository> is used to provide a list of parts and their associated properties.
toolRepository.title: General

toolsList.definition: The element <toolsList> is used to list both special and common tools and test equipment required to maintain the equipment as indicated in the maintenance allocation. When tools and test equipment are indicated in the maintenance allocation, the tools list must be included. The tools list includes a required element <title> and a required and repeatable element <toolsListGroup>.
toolsList.title: Tools list

toolsListGroup.definition: The element <toolsListGroup> is used to capture data about the tool or test equipment. It includes elements for tools list code, maintenance, nomenclature, NSN, and tool number.
toolsListGroup.title: Tools list group

toolSpec.definition: The element <toolSpec> represents a tool. It contains its associated properties.
toolSpec.title: Tool specification

toolsRefs.definition: The element <toolsRefs> is used to contain a reference to a required tool or test equipment that is contained in the tools list within the maintenance allocation data.
toolsRefs.title: Tools References

trade.definition: The element <trade> contains the typed in required trade code of the person. Care must be taken when using this element when the product is, for example, multi-national or multi-customer. The trade or trade code or both is typed in.
trade.title: Trade/trade code

transport.definition: The element <transport> contains information about the transport of the supply.
transport.title: Transport

transverseLink.definition: The transverse link element <transverseLink> provides information about internally or externally realized electrical connections of different contacts/bolts of equipment, eg terminal strips.
transverseLink.title: Transverse link

triaxialCableFlag.definition: The element <triaxialCableFlag> identifies tri-axial cables. In many cases, a tri-axial cable is indicated by the letter "Y" in the element content.
triaxialCableFlag.title: Tri-axial information

trigger.definition: The element <trigger> provides the means to establish that the inspection must be performed after a certain event.
trigger.title: Trigger

twist.definition: The element <twist> and its attribute twistingType contain information about the twisting of a wire. The element <twist> must contain all twist information of the wire. The available twisting type attribute twistingType specifies the type of twisting in coded form. Twist information can be different on both sides of a wire. The element <twist> must contain the twist information on this side of the wire.
twist.title: Twist information

twistGroup.definition: The twisting of twisted wires element <twistGroup> is used as a container for the subordinate twist information elements.
twistGroup.title: Twisting of twisted wires

unitOfIssue.definition: The element <unitOfIssue > is used to store Unit of Issue (UOI) information. The unit of issue is used to indicate the physical measurement, count or container in which the item is issued.
unitOfIssue.title: Unit of issue

unitOfIssueQualificationSegment.definition: The element <unitOfIssueQualificationSegment> is used to identify a S2000M Unit of Issue Qualification Segment (PCS) segment.
unitOfIssueQualificationSegment.title: PCS data

unverified.definition: The element <unverified> identifies that the data module which has not yet been first verified.
unverified.title: Unverified

usableOnCodeAssy.definition: The element <usableOnCodeAssy> is used to record the assembly variants and configurations variants to which the item is applied.
usableOnCodeAssy.title: Usable on code assembly

usableOnCodeEquip.definition: The element <usableOnCodeEquip> is used to record the equipment variants and configurations to which the item is applied.
usableOnCodeEquip.title: Usable on code equipment

usage.definition: The element <usage> contains the supply requirement alternative usage description.
usage.title: Usage

usageCategory.definition: This element is used to store, through its attribute, the usage category of the part, (manufacturer proprietary part, standards part, etc). Definition of the usage category values is up to the project.
usageCategory.title: Part usage category

userEntry.definition: A user entry dialog receives data input by the user.
userEntry.title: User dialog entry

validate.definition: The element <validate> is used for validating the user entry thru an expression evaluation (refer to Para 2.4.4) of the input information.
validate.title: Validate user entry

variable.definition: Variables define pieces of information required by the logic engine to context filter, branch, etc within a process data module.
variable.title: Variables

variableDeclarations.definition: Variable declarations define and can initialize one to many variables that are used within the process data module. All variables used in a process data module must be declared within it. As of this writing, all variables are global in scope.
variableDeclarations.title: Variable declarations

variablePostSet.definition: The element <variablePostSet> mirrors the element <variablePreSet>. It contains an assertion and assigns a value to a variable after the element <dmNode> has been traversed. For example, a variablePostSet could be used on a step to apply power to assert to the state table that power has been applied for future reference by the logic engine.
variablePostSet.title: Variable post set

variablePreSet.definition: The element <variablePreSet> assigns a value to a variable before the element <dmNode> is traversed. The element <variablePreSet> contains the element <assertion>. An assertion contains the element <variableRef> and the element <expression>. The element <variableRef> has the attribute variableName, which is the name of the variable to receive the expression resulting value. When a variablePreSet is encountered in the data, the logic engine evaluates the expression and assigns the resulting value to the variable named in the element <variableRef>. For example, a variablePreSet could be used on a dmNode with an external application call to assign values to one or more of the parameter variables to be passed to the application.
variablePreSet.title: Variable pre set

verbatimText.definition: The element <verbatimText> contains text that is supposed to be presented with as little content distorting formatting applied. Typically, using the element <verbatimText>, the verbatim text is included to represent and show information like computer program text, non-proportional screen display text.
verbatimText.title: Verbatim text

voltage.definition: The element <voltage> contains the voltage information of wire material.
voltage.title: Voltage

wallThickness.definition: The element <wallThickness> contains the information of the wall thickness of a conduit.
wallThickness.title: Wall thickness

warning.definition: The element <warning> is used to contain hazard information that can cause personal injury or death.
warning.title: Warnings

warningAndCautionPara.definition: The element <warningAndCautionPara> contains the warning or caution text.
warningAndCautionPara.title: Warning and caution para

warningMalfunction.definition: The basic fault (warning or malfunction) which is part of the current correlated fault.
warningMalfunction.title: Warning or malfunction

warningsAndCautions.definition: The element <warningsAndCautions> contains the collection of warnings and cautions used within a data module. Each warning or caution is authored separately within the element <warningsAndCautions>. Warnings and cautions can be authored once in a data module and then referenced as needed.
warningsAndCautions.title: Warnings and cautions collection

wire.definition: The element <wire>, within the list of wires element <wireGroup>, contains wire information about the Product's wiring. The wires are the electrical connections between two equipment, different contacts of an equipment, etc. Electrical wires of a system are often bundled into harnesses.
wire.title: Element <wire> and child elements

wireCode.definition: The wire code element <wireCode> gives information about the type of a wire and its gauge through its child elements. If used, this element must be populated in accordance with Chap 3.9.5.2.9.2.
wireCode.title: Wire code

wireColor.definition: The color information element <wireColor> identifies the color of a wire. Normally, the color information is defined in coded form. Table 9 gives examples for the coding of color information.
wireColor.title: Color information

wireConnection.definition: The wire connection element contains connection information for the two ends of a wire. In special cases, eg wires with wireState = "pigtail" or "notactiv", only the connection of one wire end is used.
wireConnection.title: Wire connection

wireConnectionCode.definition: The wire connection code is used for generic identification of the electrical potential to which a wire end is connected. This can be the basis to arrange the ends of the wires in a specific order for graphical display purposes and to generate a connection analysis.
wireConnectionCode.title: Wire connection code

wireGauge.definition: This element contains the gauge of a wire. The measure type is given in the gauge type attribute wireGaugeType.
wireGauge.title: Wire gauge

wireIdent.definition: The wire identification element is the unique identifier of a wire in the system.
wireIdent.title: Wire identification

wireInfo.definition: The wire information element <wireInfo> contains child elements, which describe properties of the wire and other information related to the complete wire.
wireInfo.title: Wire information

wireInstallationCode.definition: This element contains the information for preparation and finishing of the wire for connection purposes.
wireInstallationCode.title: Wire installation code

wireMaterial.definition: The element <wireMaterial> is contained in the list of wire material element <wireMaterialGroup>. The list of wire material is a child element of the list of standard parts element <standardPartGroup>.
wireMaterial.title: Element <wireMaterial> and child elements

wireNumber.definition: All wires must have a wire identification number. If there is no further breakdown, by the use of the circuit code element <circuitIdent> and the wire section identification element <sectionIdent>, then the element <wireNumber> must contain the complete wire identification.
wireNumber.title: Wire identification number

wireRoute.definition: The element <wireRoute> contains lane codes for wires, which belong to a primary system and must be given a routing apart from other wires of the system.
wireRoute.title: Wire route lane code

wireSeqNumber.definition: The wire sequential number element <wireSeqNumber> contains the sequential number of a wire, which can be part of the entire wire identification.
wireSeqNumber.title: Wire sequential number

wireType.definition: This element gives information on the type of a wire. Normally, the wire type is defined in coded form. Table 7 gives examples for the coding of wire types.
wireType.title: Wire type

wiringFields.definition: The wiring data description Schema defines the major element <wiringFields>, which contains the child elements for wire data/fields description, harness data/fields description, equipment data/fields description and standard parts data/fields description.
wiringFields.title: Wiring data description Schema basic rules

workArea.definition: The element <workArea> contains a descriptive identifier of the area where work is accomplished that cannot be deduced from the names of the collection of zones.
workArea.title: Work area

xPaths.definition: To facilitate reusability of technical data, the element <xPaths> links to pieces of technical data in other modules that make up a leaning object. Specifically, the <xPaths>is a wrapper element is used to reference the content within different data modules. This allows that contains pointers to data module parts for inclusion of parts of in a data module (eg paragraphs or figures) rather than the entire data module.SCO. The path to the data module content is entered in the XPATH attribute of the <xPaths> element and should be the location for the data module. The rules for how to use <xPaths> should be explained in the business rules.
xPaths.title: xPaths

yesNoAnswer.definition: The element <yesNoAnswer> contains the selection of the two answers: Yes (element <yesAnswer>) or No (element <noAnswer>). Each of these is giving a reference to another action, to the final action (in element <isolationProcedureEnd>) or to the close-up requirements (element <closeRqmts>).
yesNoAnswer.title: Answers - Yes and no

zoneIdent.definition: Contrary to the id attribute, this element identifies semantically the zone as a result of its attributes.

zoneRef.definition: The element <zoneRef> contains the zoning information (one or more), as described in Chap 3.4. For the use of element <zoneRef> in connection with technical information repositories, refer to Chap 4.13.2.

zoneRepository.definition: This element is used to provide a list of zones and their associated properties.

zoneSide.definition: This element indicates on which side of the Product, the zone is located.

zoneSpec.definition: This element represents one zone. It contains its associated properties.

align.definition:
alignment. This attribute provides the default alignment setting for the table group (which is the horizontal position of the text within the column) and applies to all entries in the table group that do not have an alignment specified by their own align attribute, or in their parent table <row> element. The values for align are:
"left" means that the text is left justified (quad flush left)
"right" means that the text is right justified (quad flush right)
"center" means that the text is center justified (text is centered around the middle of the column)
"justify" means that the text is justified (both quad left and right)
"char" means that text is aligned to the leftmost occurrence of the value of the attribute char value. When the attribute align is set to "char", attributes char and charoff must be used. The attribute char is the single character that is used to align the text. The most common use is to align on a '.' (a full stop, or period) for decimal alignment of a column of numbers as shown in Fig 1:
align.title: Table group
align.name: align

alignCaption.definition:
sets the horizontal alignment of the text content of each <captionEntry> unless overridden by the align attribute the ancestor elements <colspec>, <spanspec>, <caption> or <captionText>. This attribute can have one of the following values:
"left", this means that the text is left justified (quad flush left),
"right", this means that the text is right justified (quad flush right),
"center", this means that the text is center justified (text is centered around the middle of the column).
alignCaption.title: Caption group
alignCaption.name: alignCaption

alignCaptionEntry.definition:
the horizontal alignment of each element <caption>. The attribute’s value
            defines the horizontal position of a caption within its element <captionEntry>, it
            does not affect the alignment of the text within a caption. The attribute can have one of the following values:- "left"- "right"- "center".
alignCaptionEntry.name: alignCaptionEntry

changeMark.name: changeMark

changeType.definition:
the type of the change. The attribute can have one of the following values:- "add" - the element is added- "modify" - the element is changed-
            "delete" - the element is deletedNoteThe attribute changeType can apply to any
            element and not especially to the element where the change occurs. Depending on the type
            of the change, propagation rules defining the change marking inheritance from the upper
            element to the lower can differ:- Elements marked with the value “modify” are
            allowed to contain elements marked with values “add”, “modify” or “delete”-
            Elements marked with the value “delete”: There is no need to set the change attributes
            on the element’s children because this is implied. Any change markings on child elements
            are ignored by the presentation system.- Elements marked with value “add”: There is
            no need to set the change attributes on the element’s children because this is implied.
            Any change markings on child elements are ignored by the presentation
            system.NoteIf this attribute is not used, and the attribute changeMark is
            used, the change is assumed to be an addition.

colwidth.definition:
is the column width setting. Column width can be specified using either ar proportional measure, a fixed measure, or a mixed measure.
A proportional measure is of the form "number*" (eg 10*), and means that the column width is the number times the proportion.
A fixed measure is of the form number and unit (eg 25pt, 25mm, 16.2in). The units are case insensitive and can be "pt" (points), "cm" (centimeters), "mm" (millimeters), "pi" (picas), and "in" (inches). The default fixed unit should be interpreted as "pt" if neither a proportion nor a fixed unit is specified. An example of a mixed measure is 10*+3pt.
If no column width is specified for a column specification, this implies that the column has the proportional width "1*", and hence, if no column widths are specified for any column, the column widths will be the same for each column and will be an equal proportion of the available width.
colwidth.title: Column specification

issueType.definition:
This attribute gives the issue status of the data module. There are eight values that can be used.
"new". Data modules up to and including the initial issue of the approved release must have the attribute issueNumber set to the value "000" for inwork versions or value "001" for the initial issue and have the attribute issueType set to the value "new".
"deleted". Deletion of data modules is treated as a special case of update. The data module, itself is not physically deleted from the CSDB but marked as deleted by setting the attribute issueType to the value "deleted".
"changed". Data modules that have been changed and have the changes indicated within the data module using change elements and attributes, must have the attribute issueType set to the value "changed".
"revised". Data modules that have been totally revised and that contain no change elements or attributes must have the attribute issueType set to the value "revised".
"status". Data modules that have had their identification and status information updated must have the attribute issueType set to the value "status".
"rinstate-status". Data modules that have been reinstated from a previously deleted data module and have only the status information changed must have the attribute issueType set to the value "rinstate-status". In the simplest case, this status change must require setting the attribute issueType to the value "rinstate-status".
"rinstate-changed". Data modules that have been reinstated from a previously deleted data module and have the changes indicated by change elements and attributes, must have the attribute issueType set to the value "rinstate-changed".
"rinstate-revised". Data modules that have been reinstated from a previously deleted data module and have the changes not indicated by change elements and attributes, must have the attribute issueType set to the value "rinstate-revised".
issueType.title: Status part
issueType.name: issueType

linkShow.definition:
specifies the link appearance, if an xlink link is established. Refer to 7.4.1.1. This attribute can have one of the following values:
"newPane" will open another window for the referenced data allowing the user to view the reference alongside the current data.
"embedInContext" will display the linked data inline at the point where the dmRef occurred. This is useful when you have data that can be used verbatim in several data modules and maintained in a separate data module to itself.
"replaceAndReturnToSource" will replace the current screen of data with the dmRef data and then return the user to the origin of the dmRef when he presses Next to continue. This is normal reference handling where the user views the reference and then returns to the original procedure.
"replaceAndNoReturn" will replace the current screen of data with the dmRef data and not provide a Next option. "replaceAndNoReturn" conceptually breaks the connection with the referencing data. It is useful in a troubleshooting situation when the fault has been isolated, the user is referenced to a remedy, and there is no reason for him to return to the troubleshooting procedure.

            gauge type is measured in a metric unit
wireGaugeType.name: wireGaugeType

wireInstallationDirection.definition: contains direction information for non-symmetric wires
wireInstallationDirection.title: Contact identification

wireLengthType.definition:
the type of wire length information. The following values are available:
"critical", indicates that the new wire must have exactly this defined length when a wire change is performed. Otherwise, the data delivered through the wire will not be accurate
"estimated", indicates that the wire length corresponds with the cut length without any constraints to the final length (after installation of the wire)
"final", indicates that the wire length corresponds with the length after installation of the wire
wireLengthType.title: Length information
wireLengthType.name: wireLengthType

wireState.definition:
the electrical state of a wire. Normally, wires are divided into physical electrical wires and logical connections, eg the connection of a circuit breaker to the bus bar by a screw. This attribute can have only one of the following values:
"active" for wires which are active in one of the systems circuits
"stowed" for wires which are stowed (not connected) at least on one end
"pigtail" for wires which are connected only at one end to an equipment of the system for measurement purposes
"notactiv" for wires which are not active in one of the systems circuits
"logconn" for electrical connections in one of the systems circuits which are not realized by a physical wire or do not have wire identification (in some cases called flying leads)
wireState.title: Element <wire> and child elements

worthinessLimit.definition: this attribute signifies whether the task is subject to worthiness limitations. It indicates whether the performance of the tasks is mandatory or recommended.
worthinessLimit.title: Task definition

year.definition: A four digit number, which is the year of issue.

yearOfDataIssue.definition: the year (YYYY) when the issue was raised

zoneRefType.definition: the type of the relationship between the two zones

zoneSideValue.definition:
the side of the Product where the zone is located. This attribute can have one of the following values:
"lh" for a zone located on the left side of the Product
"rh" for a zone located on the right side of the Product
"lr" when the zone is not located on one side of the Product
